links.outcome: LLM risk attribution changes across sex and race in demographic-varied prompts
links.effect: LLM attributed higher cardiovascular risk to men than women and to Black than white patients across most neutral prompts; sex-based decisions changed in two of six domains; race-based decisions stable.
links.quote: The LLM attributed higher cardiovascular risk to men than women, and to Black rather than white patients, across most neutral prompts.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM outputs across repeated runs
links.effect: Agreement across repeated runs was strong (ICC 0.949, 95% CI 0.819-0.992, p<0.001).
links.quote: Agreement across repeated runs was strong (ICC of 0.949, 95% CI: 0.819-0.992, p = <0.001).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation measuring demographic bias and variability in an LLM's cardiovascular risk attribution using simulated prompts/vignettes without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
